main_point.en: The cure for our worry and anxiety is faith in God's ability to care for us.
main_point.zh-Hant: 醫治憂慮和焦慮的方法，是相信神有能力照顧我們。

christ_connection.en: Jesus is the great Provider. He takes care of all our needs, especially our need to be rescued from sin, guilt, and death. Through His sacrifice on the cross, we are forgiven and have new life in Him.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 耶穌是偉大的供應者。祂照顧我們一切的需要，特別是我們需要從罪、罪疚和死亡中得救。藉著祂在十字架上的犧牲，我們得蒙赦免，並在祂裏面得著新生命。

title.en: Worldly Wealth Can’t Give Us Peace
title.zh-Hant: 世上的財富不能給我們平安

content.en:
13 Someone in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.” 
14 But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or arbitrator over you?” 
15 And he said to them, “Take care, and be on your guard against all covetousness, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.” 
16 And he told them a parable, saying, “The land of a rich man produced plentifully, 
17 and he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, for I have nowhere to store my crops?’ 
18 And he said, ‘I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. 
19 And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry.”’ 
20 But God said to him, ‘Fool! This night your soul is required of you, and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?’ 
21 So is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
content.zh-Hant:
13 眾人中有一個人對耶穌說：「夫子！請你吩咐我的兄長和我分開家業。」
14 耶穌說：「你這個人！誰立我作你們斷事的官，給你們分家業呢？」
15 於是對眾人說：「你們要謹慎自守，免去一切的貪心，因為人的生命不在乎家道豐富。」
16 就用比喻對他們說：「有一個財主田產豐盛；
17 自己心裏思想說：『我的出產沒有地方收藏，怎麼辦呢？』
18 又說：『我要這麼辦：要把我的倉房拆了，另蓋更大的，在那裏好收藏我一切的糧食和財物，
19 然後要對我的靈魂說：靈魂哪，你有許多財物積存，可作多年的費用，只管安安逸逸地吃喝快樂吧！』
20 神卻對他說：『無知的人哪，今夜必要你的靈魂；你所預備的要歸誰呢？』
21 凡為自己積財，在神面前卻不富足的，也是這樣。」

title.en: Seeking God’s Kingdom Gives Us Peace
title.zh-Hant: 尋求神的國使我們得平安

content.en:
22 And he said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on. 
23 For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing. 
24 Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storehouse nor barn, and yet God feeds them. Of how much more value are you than the birds! 
25 And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to his span of life? 
26 If then you are not able to do as small a thing as that, why are you anxious about the rest? 
27 Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. 
28 But if God so clothes the grass, which is alive in the field today, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith! 
29 And do not seek what you are to eat and what you are to drink, nor be worried. 
30 For all the nations of the world seek after these things, and your Father knows that you need them. 
31 Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be added to you. 
32 Fear not, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom. 
33 Sell your possessions, and give to the needy. Provide yourselves with moneybags that do not grow old, with a treasure in the heavens that does not fail, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys. 
34 For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.”
content.zh-Hant:
22 耶穌又對門徒說：「所以我告訴你們，不要為生命憂慮吃甚麼，為身體憂慮穿甚麼；
23 因為生命勝於飲食，身體勝於衣裳。
24 你想烏鴉，也不種也不收，又沒有倉又沒有庫，神尚且養活牠。你們比飛鳥是何等地貴重呢！
25 你們哪一個能用思慮使壽數多加一刻呢？
26 這最小的事，你們尚且不能做，為甚麼還憂慮其餘的事呢？
27 你想百合花怎麼長起來；它也不勞苦，也不紡線。然而我告訴你們，就是所羅門極榮華的時候，他所穿戴的，還不如這花一朵呢！
28 你們這小信的人哪，野地裏的草今天還在，明天就丟在爐裏，神還給它這樣的妝飾，何況你們呢！
29 你們不要求吃甚麼，喝甚麼，也不要掛心；
30 這都是外邦人所求的。你們必須用這些東西，你們的父是知道的。
31 你們只要求他的國，這些東西就必加給你們了。
32 你們這小群，不要懼怕，因為你們的父樂意把國賜給你們。
33 你們要變賣所有的賙濟人，為自己預備永不壞的錢囊，用不盡的財寶在天上，就是賊不能近、蟲不能蛀的地方。
34 因為，你們的財寶在哪裏，你們的心也在那裏。」

content.en: Leaders: Consider listening to “O Great God” by Sovereign Grace Music, reflecting on God’s great love and care for us.
content.zh-Hant: 領袖：可以考慮聆聽 Sovereign Grace Music 的〈O Great God〉，思想神對我們偉大的愛和照顧。

title.en: Worldly Wealth Can’t Give Us Peace
title.zh-Hant: 世上的財富不能給我們平安

content.en: “Jesus pinpoints the real motivating factor behind this appeal for justice. ... Then, as now, a person’s happiness and well-being was often thought to be determined by what he or she owned. Jesus flatly rejects this as a standard for measuring the worth of one’s life.”¹⁵
content.zh-Hant: 「耶穌指出這項伸張公義的請求背後真正的動機。……無論當時還是現在，人們往往認為一個人的幸福和福祉取決於他的財產。耶穌斷然拒絕以此作為衡量一個人生命價值的標準。」¹⁵

content.en: “This parable is about the danger of greed, measured by the abundance of possessions (v. 15). The rich man was infatuated with hoarding his ‘goods.’ In his self-centered perspective (there are at least ten self-references in vv. 17-19), he thought this was an effective strategy for a long life of leisure and pleasure. But God views such an outlook as foolish and shortsighted.”¹⁶
content.zh-Hant: 「這個比喻講述貪婪的危險；貪婪以財物的豐富為衡量標準（15節）。財主一心囤積自己的『財物』。從他以自我為中心的角度看來（17至19節中至少有十次提到自己），他認為這是長久享受安逸和快樂的有效策略。但神認為這樣的眼光愚昧又短視。」¹⁶

title.en: Seeking God’s Kingdom Gives Us Peace
title.zh-Hant: 尋求神的國使我們得平安

content.en: “The world is full of worry. We’re tempted to think that worrying is the same thing as thinking or planning or even protecting ourselves. But worry is completely useless and ineffective when it comes to adding to our life. We can’t even add one minute by worrying. The Lord calls adding a minute to our lives a little thing! So if we can’t add a minute to our lives by worry, why do we think things like protecting our children, getting good jobs, ending war, or making our neighborhoods safe will be done by worry? These are all good things, but not things that can be addressed by worry.”¹⁷
content.zh-Hant: 「世界充滿憂慮。我們很容易以為憂慮等同於思考、計劃，甚至保護自己。但憂慮對延長我們的生命完全無用，也毫無成效。我們不能靠憂慮使生命多一分鐘。主稱使生命多一分鐘為一件小事！既然我們不能靠憂慮使生命多一分鐘，為甚麼還以為憂慮能保護兒女、找到好工作、結束戰爭，或使社區安全呢？這些都是好事，但都不是靠憂慮能解決的。」¹⁷

content.en: “If God is truly looking after the material needs of the birds, then how much more would he care for the genuine needs of those who are far more valuable to him—those who are in a relationship with his Son! Worrying cannot contribute anything to one’s well-being. Obviously, worrying cannot increase one’s life span. Recent studies by psychologists reinforce Jesus’s teaching on the counter-productive effects of worry on longevity.”¹⁸
content.zh-Hant: 「如果神確實照顧飛鳥物質上的需要，那麼祂豈不更會照顧那些在祂眼中貴重得多的人——與祂兒子有關係的人——的真正需要嗎？憂慮對人的福祉毫無幫助。顯然，憂慮不能延長人的壽命。心理學家近期的研究進一步印證耶穌的教導：憂慮對壽命有反效果。」¹⁸

content.en: Rabbis often settled disputes in Jewish culture, and since many people recognized Jesus as a rabbi, this man’s question about inheritance makes sense. But Jesus refused to get caught up in such a small dispute. He came to settle a greater question—one of life and death—with eternal consequences. Jesus’s purpose wasn’t about earthly inheritance. Jesus came for the spiritually sick so those dying from sin (everyone) could know the only way to be healed: through faith in Him Mark 2:17; Luke 5:32; John 14:6). Jesus’s mission was about more than monetary inheritance among brothers; it was about the spiritual inheritance people would receive as coheirs with Christ if they trusted Him for salvation. Make no mistake: Jesus is a righteous Judge, and one day He will judge all people. But this is not a judgment believers should fear. He has covered us fully and finally with His blood—and we are judged not by our own works but by His. Charles Spurgeon said it this way: “If we trust him with our souls, he will not give us a bare salvation but a rich robe of righteousness to cover all our [sin].”"9 God never does things halfway; everything He gives us is the best; the best evidence is Jesus’s perfect sacrifice on our behalf. We can trust that our salvation is secure in Him. The dispute between us and God was settled on the cross through Jesus’s blood.
content.zh-Hant: 在猶太文化中，拉比經常調解糾紛；既然許多人認耶穌為拉比，這人提出有關產業的問題也就不難理解。但耶穌不肯捲入這樣的小糾紛。祂來是要解決一個更重大的問題——攸關生死、帶來永恆後果的問題。耶穌的目的並非地上的產業。耶穌為靈裏有病的人而來，使因罪而死亡的人（也就是所有人）知道唯一得醫治的方法：相信祂（馬可福音 2:17；路加福音 5:32；約翰福音 14:6）。耶穌的使命不只是關乎兄弟之間的金錢產業，更關乎人若信靠祂得救，就能與基督一同承受的屬靈產業。不要誤會：耶穌是公義的審判者，終有一天祂要審判所有人。但信徒不必懼怕這審判。祂用自己的寶血完全而永遠地遮蓋了我們；我們受審判的依據不是自己的行為，而是祂的作為。查理·司布真這樣說：「我們若把靈魂交託給祂，祂不會只給我們救恩而已，還會給我們一件華美的公義外袍，遮蓋我們一切的[罪]。」⁹ 神做事從不敷衍了事；祂給我們的一切都是最好的；最好的證據就是耶穌為我們獻上的完美祭。救恩在祂裏面穩妥可靠，我們可以信靠祂。我們與神之間的爭議，已藉著耶穌的寶血在十字架上解決了。

content.en: Adoption into God’s family is one of the positive benefits of justification. Not only are we freed from the judgment against us through justification, but we also experience a change of identity—we become children of God (John 1:12; Gal. 4:5). Through adoption our relationship with God, which was once lost through the fall, is now restored, resulting in the benefits of being an heir of God and a coheir with Christ (Rom. 8:16-17).
content.zh-Hant: 被收納進神的家是稱義所帶來的積極福分之一。藉著稱義，我們不僅從對我們的審判中得釋放，身分也改變了——我們成為神的兒女（約翰福音 1:12；加拉太書 4:5）。藉著蒙收納，我們與神曾因墮落而失去的關係如今得以恢復，並因此得享作神的後嗣、與基督同作後嗣的福分（羅馬書 8:16-17）。

content.en: LORD, FORGIVE ME FOR THE TIMES WHEN I LET MY WORRY RULE MY LIFE. I CRAVE YOUR PEACE FOR MYSELF AND MY STUDENTS. PLEASE HELP ME TO REFOCUS MY HEART ON YOU, TRUSTING YOU WITH EVERYTHING. GUIDE ME TO SHOW MY STUDENTS HOW TO DO THE SAME.
content.zh-Hant: 主啊，求祢赦免我讓憂慮支配生活的時候。我渴望自己和學生都得著祢的平安。求祢幫助我重新把心轉向祢，將一切交託給祢。求祢引導我向學生示範如何同樣信靠祢。

content.en: On a scale of 1 to 10 (1=Never; 10=All the time), how often would you say you feel anxious?
content.zh-Hant: 以一至十分評分（一分代表從不，十分代表一直如此），你覺得自己多常感到焦慮？

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You'll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些可選活動旨在幫助學生互動，包括一個討論活動和一個文化連結，後者涉及當今青少年文化中的相關話題。每個小組都不一樣，請調整活動以配合小組的需要。目的是讓學生在與話題和彼此建立連結時，更投入這一課。

提出以下問題，留時間讓學生分享答案：

question.en: WHAT CAUSES ANXIETY?
question.zh-Hant: 甚麼會引起焦慮？

question.en: WHAT'S THE MOST “NORMAL,” EVERYDAY THING YOU WORRY ABOUT? WHAT’S THE STRANGEST?
question.zh-Hant: 你擔心過最「平常」的日常事情是甚麼？最奇怪的又是甚麼？

question.en: HOW DO YOU FIGHT FEELINGS OF WORRY OR ANXIETY?
question.zh-Hant: 你怎樣對抗憂慮或焦慮的感覺？

content.en: Most of us worry about something—whether it’s our family, friends, grades, sports or band performances, or making it to work on time after school. Having a plan and being responsible are good, but worry and anxiety aren’t healthy for us. Jesus provides a better way. He shows that trusting God to provide all we need is the ultimate cure for worry and anxiety.
content.zh-Hant: 我們大多數人都有擔心的事——可能是家人、朋友、成績、運動表現或樂隊演出，或放學後能否準時上班。有計劃、有責任感是好的，但憂慮和焦慮對我們不健康。耶穌提供了更好的道路。祂指出，信靠神供應我們一切所需，是醫治憂慮和焦慮的根本方法。

cultural_connection.en: What do you do, who do you look for, and where do you go when you want a moment of peace? Some of us might try deep breathing, venting to or crying with a close friend or family member, or spending time in nature. None of those things are wrong, but they simply aren’t enough. At times, the world around us seems to spin out of control. Because we can’t do anything to stop it, we stress, worry, and let anxiety steal our peace. No matter what we’re facing in the moment, we can’t solve anything with stress or worry. Or, as Jesus asks, can you really make your life any better by worrying (Luke 12:25)? Of course, the answer is “no.” Our worry can’t give us anything and can only steal from us—our peace, joy, self-discipline, and even our sense of security. But worry’s biggest flaw? It takes our eyes off Jesus. When our eyes move away from our compassionate Savior, through whom God has provided for our greatest need, we sink. Thankfully, Jesus is always ready to catch us and keep us from drowning (Matt. 14:28-31). When we trust Him, we have everything we need.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 當你想要片刻平靜時，你會做甚麼、找誰、到哪裏去？有些人可能會嘗試深呼吸、向親近的朋友或家人傾訴或與他們一同哭泣，或花時間走進大自然。這些都沒有錯，卻不足夠。有時我們周圍的世界彷彿失去控制。因為無法阻止，我們便感到壓力和憂慮，讓焦慮奪走平安。無論當下面對甚麼，壓力或憂慮都不能解決問題。正如耶穌所問，憂慮真的能讓你的生命變得更好嗎（路加福音 12:25）？答案當然是「不能」。憂慮不能給我們任何東西，只會奪走我們的平安、喜樂、自律，甚至安全感。但憂慮最大的問題是甚麼？它使我們的目光離開耶穌。當我們不再仰望這位滿有憐憫的救主，就是神藉著祂供應我們最大需要的那一位，我們便會下沉。感謝主，耶穌隨時準備接住我們，免得我們溺斃（馬太福音 14:28-31）。信靠祂，我們就有一切所需。

title.en: Worldly Wealth Can’T Give Us Peace
title.zh-Hant: 世上的財富不能給我們平安

question.en: Would people today say the rich man was holding on to things that didn’t matter or living the good life? What do you think?
question.zh-Hant: 今天的人會說這個財主緊抓著不重要的東西，還是說他過著美好的生活？你怎麼看？

answer.en: Many people today consider “the good life” as having everything they want. So, they pursue money and belongings, popularity and relaxation, academic success and fun experiences. None of these things are wrong; enjoying what God has given us and using it wisely is good. But nothing can bring us peace like God Himself. As Jesus pointed out, pursuing God’s glory and building His kingdom matter most. He should be the heart and focus behind everything we have and do. The good life, then, from a biblical perspective is pursuing God, who is good and wants what’s best for us.
answer.zh-Hant: 今天許多人認為「美好的生活」就是擁有一切想要的東西。因此，他們追求金錢和財物、人氣和安逸、學業成就和有趣的經歷。這些本身都沒有錯；享受神賜給我們的東西並明智地使用，是好的。但沒有甚麼能像神自己一樣帶給我們平安。正如耶穌指出的，追求神的榮耀、建立祂的國最為重要。祂應當是我們所擁有和所做一切背後的核心和焦點。因此，從聖經的角度看，美好的生活就是追求良善、願意將最好的賜給我們的神。

question.en: What do we turn to for security or comfort? Where did Jesus say we will and won’t find security?
question.zh-Hant: 我們向甚麼尋求安全感或安慰？耶穌說我們在哪裏能找到或找不到安全感？

answer.en: We look to all kinds of things for security and comfort, like our favorite people, our family’s money and influence, our grades or athletic achievements, even our go-to foods, music, or hoodies when we have a bad day. The man in this story looked to his inheritance for security, but Jesus pointed him to being “rich toward God” (v. 21). We won’t find security in anything or anyone here on earth; we find security in God, in using every gift and resource He gives us to glorify Him and build His kingdom. Our efforts can’t bring us security in God—Jesus does. Through His sacrifice on the cross, God adopted us into His family, and the Holy Spirit living within us guarantees our eternal security.
answer.zh-Hant: 我們向各種事物尋求安全感和安慰，例如我們最喜愛的人、家人的金錢和影響力、我們的成績或運動成就，甚至在日子不順心時常選擇的食物、音樂或連帽衫。故事中的人向自己的產業尋求安全感，但耶穌卻指引他，要在「神面前」成為「富足」的人（21節）。我們無法從地上的任何事物或任何人身上找到安全感；我們在神裏面找到安全感，並運用祂賜給我們的每一份恩賜和資源榮耀祂、建立祂的國。我們自己的努力不能使我們在神裏面得著安全感；只有耶穌能。藉著祂在十字架上的犧牲，神收納我們成為祂家中的一分子，住在我們裏面的聖靈確保我們永遠穩妥。

question.en: Why do we struggle with greed, envy, or worry? How can knowing that everything we have comes from God help us?
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼我們會受貪婪、嫉妒或憂慮困擾？知道我們所擁有的一切都來自神，如何幫助我們？

answer.en: Greed, envy, and anxiety creep in when we look at people to our right and to our left instead of fixing our eyes on Jesus. We desire things that don’t belong to us; we desire the gifts and blessings more than the Giver, our great God. Though we are tempted to complain about what we don’t have or about what we do have not being good enough, the truth is that everything we have ultimately comes from God. Without Him and His provision, we would have nothing at all—certainly, nothing good. As Job—a man of God who lost everything—said, God has the power to give us anything and the power to take it away. Either way, He is good. Either way, He is praiseworthy (Job 1:21). Nothing on this earth will satisfy us like He will because nothing here truly lasts. But our good, unchanging, and eternal God does. In Him, our hope rests securely. In Him, we have everything we could ever need—peace for our souls forever. This truth can help us be content here, even when we don’t have everything we want.
answer.zh-Hant: 當我們東張西望，看別人而不定睛仰望耶穌時，貪婪、嫉妒和焦慮便悄悄進入我們心中。我們渴望不屬於自己的東西；我們渴望禮物和祝福，勝過渴望賜予者——我們偉大的神。雖然我們容易抱怨自己沒有甚麼，或認為已有的不夠好，但事實是，我們擁有的一切最終都來自神。沒有祂和祂的供應，我們甚麼都不會有——肯定不會有任何好東西。正如失去一切的屬神之人約伯所說，神有權柄賜給我們任何東西，也有權柄收回。無論如何，祂都是良善的，都配得稱讚（約伯記 1:21）。地上沒有甚麼能像祂一樣使我們滿足，因為這裏沒有甚麼真正長存；但我們良善、不改變、永恆的神卻永遠長存。我們的盼望在祂裏面穩妥安定。在祂裏面，我們有一切所需——靈魂永遠的平安。這真理能幫助我們在此時此地知足，即使我們沒有得到一切想要的。

title.en: Seeking God’S Kingdom Gives Us Peace
title.zh-Hant: 尋求神的國使我們得平安

question.en: Jesus said worry isn’t good for us, so why do we stress about the details of our everyday lives?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌說憂慮對我們沒有益處，那麼為甚麼我們還會為日常生活的細節感到壓力？

answer.en: Worry isn’t helpful at all; it adds nothing to our lives. In fact, it takes away from our well-being mentally, spiritually, and physically. Science even says that worry is bad for our overall health. So, why do we do it? We could say we want control or that imagining the possible outcomes is better than not knowing. Ultimately, three things create stress: lack of trust in God, misunderstanding how much God values us, and taking our focus off Jesus. The cure for worry, then, is to move our eyes away from our stress and back to God, who is aware of and takes care of our needs, who values us so much that He sent His only Son to die to save us from our sin, and who cares about every detail of our lives—big and small.
answer.zh-Hant: 憂慮毫無幫助，不能為我們的生命增添甚麼。事實上，它損害我們心理、靈性和身體的健康。科學甚至指出憂慮有損整體健康。那我們為甚麼還要憂慮？我們可能會說，我們想掌控一切，或認為想像各種可能的結果總比不知道好。歸根究底，有三件事帶來壓力：不信靠神、不了解神多麼看重我們，以及不再定睛仰望耶穌。因此，醫治憂慮的方法是把目光從壓力轉回神身上。祂知道並照顧我們的需要，祂如此看重我們，甚至差遣獨生子受死，救我們脫離罪；祂也關心我們生活中的每個細節，無論大小。

question.en: What would be different if we viewed every moment of stress and worry as an invitation to trust God instead?
question.zh-Hant: 如果我們把每個感到壓力和憂慮的時刻，都看作信靠神的邀請，會有甚麼不同？

answer.en: Stress and worry often turn our focus inward. We want to know how to fix it, reduce it, or get out of it, right? But no matter how impossible our situation seems, God is in control. What we can control is how we look at and respond to the situation. The more we stare at the problem, the bigger it seems; the more we look to God, the more we remember His faithfulness. Setting worry aside requires a shift in perspective. Instead of looking at what’s making us feel stuck, we can choose to look to God, whose arms are open in invitation to come and see that He is good and will provide for us. When we step into His open arms, He promises we’ll find rest for our worn-out, stressed-out, burned-out souls (Matt. 11:28-30).
answer.zh-Hant: 壓力和憂慮常使我們的注意力轉向自己。我們想知道怎樣解決、減輕或擺脫它，對嗎？但無論處境看來多麼不可能，神仍掌管一切。我們能控制的是如何看待和回應處境。我們越盯著問題，問題看來就越大；我們越仰望神，就越記得祂的信實。放下憂慮需要改變眼光。我們可以選擇不再注視使自己感到受困的事，轉而仰望神。祂張開雙臂邀請我們來，親自看見祂的良善和供應。當我們投入祂張開的懷抱，祂應許我們疲憊、受壓、精疲力竭的靈魂必得安息（馬太福音 11:28-30）。

question.en: What did Jesus say would happen when we seek God’s kingdom? What did He mean?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌說我們尋求神的國時會發生甚麼事？祂的意思是甚麼？

answer.en: Jesus promised that when we seek God’s kingdom, “these things will be added to [us]” (v. 31). But hearing that we’re supposed to seek God’s kingdom doesn’t bring clarity on how to do it. Jesus gave us a few examples here. He taught us to give and serve without holding back and not to be afraid when we do because God delights in giving our minds, bodies, and souls what they need to thrive. Seeking God’s kingdom means we want and pursue God’s will in the world. So, we make Him Lord of our lives, giving Him control over every area. We ask the Holy Spirit to guide us where He wants us. And we focus on glorifying God and helping others come to know Him. When we focus on these things, we proclaim our trust in God to take care of everything else, and He does.
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌應許，當我們尋求神的國，「這些東西就必加給你們了」（31節）。但聽見我們應當尋求神的國，還不足以讓我們明白如何去做。耶穌在這裏給了我們幾個例子。祂教導我們毫無保留地給予和服事，做這些事時不要害怕，因為神樂意賜給我們的心思、身體和靈魂蓬勃成長所需的一切。尋求神的國，意思是我們渴望並追求神的旨意在世上成就。因此，我們讓祂作生命的主，把每一個領域的主權交給祂。我們求聖靈引導我們到祂要我們去的地方。我們也專注於榮耀神，幫助別人認識祂。當我們專注於這些事，就是表明我們信靠神照顧其他一切，而祂也確實如此行。

question.en: Where are you clinging to time, resources, possessions, or people because of fear or worry? How can you trust God in those areas?
question.zh-Hant: 你在哪些方面因懼怕或憂慮而緊抓著時間、資源、財物或人不放？你如何在這些方面信靠神？

answer.en: We often hold a scarcity mindset, believing what we need to survive is limited and focusing on what we don’t have rather than what we do. This mindset causes us to cling tightly to the things and people in our lives because we’re afraid of losing them. No matter how much we clench our fists around what’s “ours,” God has the final say in what stays and what goes. Because we don’t know the scope of His big plan for the world, opening our hands to Him can feel scary. But God promises we’ll have what we need because above all else, He is enough. This week, challenge yourself to let go of one small thing you’ve been holding on to—whether it’s an hour with your friends, giving beyond your tithe to support missionaries, or inviting a new person to hang out with you at lunch. God honors every effort to trust in Him. Start small and see what God will do in your heart and around you.
answer.zh-Hant: 我們常抱著匱乏的心態，認為生存所需的資源有限，只看到自己沒有的，而不是已有的。這種心態使我們緊抓著生命中的事物和人，因為害怕失去。無論我們多麼緊握「屬於我們」的東西，甚麼留下、甚麼離去，最終仍由神決定。因為我們不知道祂對世界的宏大計劃有多廣闊，向祂攤開雙手可能令人害怕。但神應許我們會有一切所需，因為祂自己超越一切，已經足夠。這星期，挑戰自己放下一件緊抓著的小事——無論是與朋友相處的一小時、在十一奉獻之外支持宣教士，還是邀請一位新朋友午餐時和你一起相聚。神看重我們每一次信靠祂的努力。從小事開始，看看神會在你心裏和你周圍做甚麼。

content.en:
Some teams and clubs are exclusive. Everyone is welcome to join but must meet certain qualifications to get in and stay in. Academic clubs require certain grades. Service clubs ask you to commit to a minimum number of volunteer hours each semester. Band requires that you have and learn to play an instrument. Drama clubs select actors who best fit the parts for their production, and choirs choose only a few vocalists to perform solos. The soccer team requires athleticism and, at the very least, the potential to become a skilled soccer player. No matter what club or team we try to join, we all want to be chosen, to find our place on the team, and to remain there throughout our school years.

While being a Christian, being part of God’s family, might sound exclusive, here’s the cool thing: Jesus met every qualification for us. God sent Him for this very reason: to live perfectly according to His law; to die in our place as the perfect, once-for-all sacrifice for sin; and to rise from the grave and offer us eternal life with Him. The only qualification to become children of God is faith—believing that Jesus is who He claims to be and trusting Him as our Savior.

In His death and resurrection, Jesus not only offers us the hope of salvation, but He also offers us a place to belong as God’s sons and daughters. No matter what our family looks like here on earth, we have a perfect heavenly Father who loves us and chose to send His own Son to die in our place so that we could be part of His family, along with all other believers—our brothers and sisters in Christ.
content.zh-Hant:
有些團隊和社團有入會門檻。雖然歡迎每個人加入，卻必須符合某些條件才能進入並留下。學術社團要求一定的成績；服務社團要求你承諾每學期至少服務一定時數；樂隊要求你有一件樂器並學習演奏。戲劇社會挑選最適合劇中角色的演員，合唱團也只會挑選少數歌手獨唱。足球隊要求運動能力，至少要有成為技術純熟球員的潛力。無論我們想加入甚麼社團或球隊，我們都想被選上，在團隊中找到自己的位置，並在求學期間一直留在其中。

成為基督徒、成為神家中的一分子，聽來或許也有門檻，但奇妙的是：耶穌已經為我們滿足所有條件。神差遣祂正是為了這個目的：完全按照神的律法生活；代替我們受死，成為完美、一次獻上就永遠有效的贖罪祭；並從墳墓中復活，賜給我們與祂同在的永生。成為神兒女唯一的條件是信心——相信耶穌的身分正如祂所宣稱的，並信靠祂作我們的救主。

藉著祂的死和復活，耶穌不僅賜給我們得救的盼望，也讓我們作神的兒女，有一個歸屬之處。無論我們在地上的家庭是甚麼樣子，我們都有一位完美的天父。祂愛我們，並選擇差遣自己的兒子代替我們受死，使我們能與所有其他信徒——我們在基督裏的弟兄姊妹——一同成為祂家中的一分子。

question.en: When have you worried that you didn’t meet the qualifications for following God? How does it help to know Jesus met all the qualifications for you?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾在甚麼時候擔心自己不符合跟隨神的條件？知道耶穌已經為你滿足所有條件，對你有甚麼幫助？

question.en: What does it look like to live like a son or daughter of God? Why do you think this is so difficult?
question.zh-Hant: 活出神兒女的樣式是怎樣的？你認為為甚麼這麼困難？

prayer.en: HEAVENLY FATHER, THANK YOU FOR SENDING YOUR SON SO WE COULD BECOME YOUR SONS AND DAUGHTERS. SHOW ME HOW TO LIVE OUT OF THAT IDENTITY AND LOVE MY BROTHERS AND SISTERS IN CHRIST.
prayer.zh-Hant: 天父，感謝祢差遣祢的兒子，使我們能成為祢的兒女。求祢教導我如何活出這個身分，並愛我在基督裏的弟兄姊妹。

content.en:
Have you ever received a discount, gift, or even special privileges because of someone you were with? Like getting an employee discount on your coffee because your best friend is the barista. Or being allowed backstage at a concert for your favorite artist because your brother works at the concert venue. Or maybe your last name kept you from getting into trouble for being in the teacher’s lounge after school because your mom is a teacher at your school. Perks of knowing the right people at the right time can allow us more freedom.

Being “in Christ”—trusting Jesus for salvation and living in the new life He offers us—provides the ultimate perks. Think about it: When we’re with the right people here on earth, we often receive extra benefits, and these things can be cool or good for us, but they’re temporary and not always necessary. But God doesn’t just provide for our daily needs; He provided for our biggest need by sending His Son. We can experience freedom from sin and receive eternal life through Jesus.

Although believers are children of God and in Christ, this doesn’t mean we’re equal with Jesus. He has always been God’s Son by nature; we are God’s children through adoption. However, because we are in Christ when we trust Him for salvation, we are Christ’s coheirs Rom. 8:17). Far greater than any discount or special privileges, as coheirs with Christ, children of God receive an inheritance of salvation, eternal life, and the kingdom of God (Eph. 1:11-14; 1 Pet. 1:3-4). We don’t do anything to deserve this inheritance, and we could never earn it; God gives it to us freely through Jesus because of His work on the cross. And no person or passing of time can ever take it away from us.
content.zh-Hant:
你曾因為與某個人在一起而得到折扣、禮物，甚至特別待遇嗎？例如，你最好的朋友是咖啡師，所以你買咖啡時得到員工折扣；或因為你的兄弟在演唱會場館工作，你獲准進入最喜愛的藝人的演唱會後台。又或者因為你的母親是學校的老師，你放學後在教師休息室時，別人看見你的姓氏就沒有追究。在適當的時候認識適當的人，所帶來的好處能給我們更多自由。

「在基督裏」——信靠耶穌得救，並活在祂賜給我們的新生命中——帶來最美好的福分。想想看：當我們在地上與適當的人在一起，往往會得到額外的好處。這些事可能很棒或對我們有益，卻是暫時的，也不一定是必需的。但神不只供應我們日常的需要；祂差遣祂的兒子，供應了我們最大的需要。藉著耶穌，我們能經歷從罪中得自由，並領受永生。

雖然信徒是神的兒女，也在基督裏，這不表示我們與耶穌平等。祂按本性從來就是神的兒子；我們則是藉著收納成為神的兒女。然而，當我們信靠基督得救，就在祂裏面，因此與祂同作後嗣（羅馬書 8:17）。作為與基督同作後嗣的人，神的兒女領受救恩、永生和神的國為產業（以弗所書 1:11-14；彼得前書 1:3-4），這遠勝任何折扣或特別待遇。我們沒有做甚麼配得這產業，也永遠無法靠自己賺取；神因耶穌在十字架上的工作，藉著祂白白賜給我們。任何人或時間的流逝都不能奪走它。

question.en: What comes to mind when you think of inheritance? How is our inheritance in Christ better?
question.zh-Hant: 想到產業時，你會想到甚麼？我們在基督裏的產業好在哪裏？

question.en: Why is it important for us to remember that we are coheirs with Christ but not equals?
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼我們必須記得，自己雖與基督同作後嗣，卻不與祂平等？

prayer.en: GOD, YOU ARE A GOOD FATHER. YOU HAVE PROVIDED FOR ME BEYOND WHAT I CAN IMAGINE, FULFILLING MY GREATEST NEED IN JESUS, YOUR SON. THANK YOU FOR WHAT YOU’VE GIVEN ME NOW AND FOR MY FUTURE INHERITANCE.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，祢是良善的父。祢給我的供應超過我的想像，在祢兒子耶穌裏滿足了我最大的需要。感謝祢現在賜給我的一切，以及將來要給我的產業。

content.en:
We all know what it’s like to feel stuck—whether it’s a fallen log that makes a trail impassable, a problem on a math test that seems unsolvable, or a defensive line you worry you can’t break through. In these moments, we look around for another path, another solution, or a weakness in the defense so we can make our way forward and move toward the goal. Life finds us in lots of places where we feel worn down or even hopeless because we can’t see a way forward, but God promises to make our path clear when we trust in Him.

Here’s the thing: God makes a way through what seems impossible to us because nothing is impossible to Him. All of us were once stuck in our sin and needed His rescue (Rom. 3:23), so He sent Jesus to redeem us, to free us from our sin. Jesus plainly says He is the only way for us to be saved from our sin and have a restored relationship with God. This is a clear answer to our greatest question, but God is good and kind and doesn’t leave us to figure out life in Christ on our own.

Through His Word and His Spirit, God is our ever-present Protector and Guide who doesn’t abandon us even when life feels uncertain but shows us “the path of life” and “fullness of joy” in Him (Ps. 16:11). He promises that when we trust Him and put His will and Word above our own, He will show us clearly which way to go (Prov. 3:5-6). No matter how overwhelming life feels right now, God is right there, walking with you through your stress and pain. Trust Him to guide you; know that He will hold you securely all the way through (Ps. 16:8; John 10:28-30).

God, right now I feel stuck, and I need You to show me the way forward. Help me to rest securely in You and Your wisdom as You guide me forward on the best path.
content.zh-Hant:
我們都知道受困的感覺——無論是倒下的樹幹使小徑無法通行、數學考試中一道似乎解不開的題目，或是你擔心自己無法突破的防守陣線。在這些時刻，我們會四處尋找另一條路、另一種解法，或防守的弱點，好讓自己能繼續前進，朝目標邁進。生活中有許多時候，我們因看不到前路而感到疲憊，甚至絕望；但神應許，當我們信靠祂，祂會為我們指明道路。

事實是，神能在我們看似不可能的處境中開路，因為在祂沒有難成的事。我們都曾困在罪中，需要祂拯救（羅馬書 3:23），所以祂差遣耶穌救贖我們，使我們從罪中得自由。耶穌清楚說明，祂是我們從罪中得救、與神恢復關係的唯一道路。這是我們最大問題的明確答案；但神良善仁慈，祂不會讓我們獨自摸索如何在基督裏生活。

藉著祂的話語和聖靈，神是時刻與我們同在的保護者和引導者。即使生活令人感到不確定，祂也不會離棄我們，反而向我們指示「生命的道路」，使我們在祂面前有「滿足的喜樂」（詩篇 16:11）。祂應許，當我們信靠祂，把祂的旨意和話語放在自己之上，祂會清楚指示我們該走的路（箴言 3:5-6）。無論此刻生活的壓力多麼沉重，神就在那裏，陪伴你走過壓力和痛苦。信靠祂的引導；要知道祂會一路穩穩地扶持你（詩篇 16:8；約翰福音 10:28-30）。

神啊，現在我覺得自己困住了，需要祢為我指明前路。求祢引導我走最好的路，幫助我安穩地倚靠祢和祢的智慧。

question.en: How would you describe what it means to trust God with all your heart? Are you doing that? Why or why not?
question.zh-Hant: 你會怎樣形容全心信靠神的意思？你正在這樣做嗎？為甚麼？

question.en: Where do you need God to show you the way forward right now? What would it look like for you to ask Him for help?
question.zh-Hant: 現在你需要神在哪方面為你指明前路？你可以怎樣向祂求助？

prayer.en: God, right now I feel stuck, and I need You to show me the way forward. Help me to rest securely in You and Your wisdom as You guide me forward on the best path.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，現在我覺得自己困住了，需要祢為我指明前路。求祢引導我走最好的路，幫助我安穩地倚靠祢和祢的智慧。

content.en:
Think about how much less intimidating darkness feels once someone flips the light switch. Or how much less you stumble over your feet on a trail or sidewalk once someone turns on the flashlight. Or even how much clearer photos turn out if enough light filters through the lens. Light makes a difference in the way we see everything—in what we see.

Let’s be real: Sin and evil in the world around us and in our own lives can sometimes make life seem really dark. And the darker life gets, the more we struggle to cling to hope. We begin to wonder if things will ever change or why God hasn’t changed them already. Truly, God made us for a world full of light, full of hope, full of Him, so it’s no surprise that we feel uncomfortable in the darkness. But because of sin, we’re here. So, how do we live as “children of light” John 12:36; 1 Thess. 5:5)? How do we hold on to hope, even during the darkest days? We turn our eyes to Jesus—the Light of the world (John 8:12).

Jesus is the light that shines in the darkness and can’t be overcome (John 1:4-5); His light is life. He is our hope and steadying anchor when the rest of life seems hopeless and chaotic Heb. 6:19). And this hope will never fail because it is secured in the blood of Jesus Himself and sealed with the presence of the Holy Spirit within us (Rom. 5:5). Although these dark days may seem pointless to us, God uses them to refine us and produce godly character in us. No matter how crushed, persecuted, or weighed down we might feel, we are never without hope— because we are never without Him (2 Cor. 4:8-9).
content.zh-Hant:
想想看，一旦有人打開電燈，黑暗是不是少了許多可怕？或者有人打開手電筒後，你在小徑或人行道上是不是比較不容易絆倒？又或者足夠的光線進入鏡頭，照片是不是清晰得多？光會改變我們看萬事的方式，也改變我們所看見的。

說實話，我們周圍世界和自己生命中的罪惡，有時會使生活看起來十分黑暗。生活越黑暗，我們越難緊握盼望。我們開始懷疑事情是否會改變，或神為甚麼還沒有改變這一切。的確，神造我們是為了生活在充滿光、充滿盼望、充滿祂同在的世界裏，所以我們在黑暗中感到不自在並不奇怪。但因著罪，我們身處黑暗。那麼，我們如何活得像「光明之子」（約翰福音 12:36；帖撒羅尼迦前書 5:5）？即使在最黑暗的日子，我們如何持守盼望？我們要把目光轉向耶穌——世界的光（約翰福音 8:12）。

耶穌是在黑暗中照耀、不能被勝過的光（約翰福音 1:4-5）；祂的光就是生命。當生活的其他方面看似毫無盼望、混亂不堪時，祂是我們的盼望和使我們穩固的錨（希伯來書 6:19）。這盼望永不落空，因為它由耶穌自己的寶血確保，並以住在我們裏面的聖靈作印記（羅馬書 5:5）。雖然這些黑暗的日子在我們看來可能毫無意義，神卻用它們來煉淨我們，在我們裏面塑造敬虔的品格。無論我們感到多麼被壓傷、受逼迫或負擔沉重，我們絕不會沒有盼望——因為我們絕不會沒有祂（哥林多後書 4:8-9）。

question.en: Where has the light of Jesus made the most difference in your life lately?
question.zh-Hant: 最近耶穌的光在哪方面為你的生活帶來最大的改變？

question.en: How do you need Jesus’s light to bring hope to the dark places in your life right now?
question.zh-Hant: 現在你需要耶穌的光如何為你生命中黑暗的地方帶來盼望？

prayer.en: LORD JESUS, YOU ARE MY LIGHT WHEN THE WORLD AROUND ME SEEMS DARK. HELP ME TO CLING TO THE HOPE I HAVE IN YOU, KEEPING MY EYES FIXED ON YOU AND THE HOPE OF SALVATION.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主耶穌，當我周圍的世界看似黑暗時，祢是我的光。求祢幫助我緊握在祢裏面的盼望，定睛仰望祢和得救的盼望。

content.en:
Today, we often struggle to determine what we want versus what we need. We might say we need things like new clothes or shoes when our old ones fit but aren’t in style; a smartphone; social media; a new car when our car’s paint is peeling, but it runs well; or a favorite soda instead of water. However, when we get down to the basics, our needs are pretty straightforward: food, water, a place to live, clothing, sleep and rest, and connection with others.

Jesus sums up our needs in three questions we ask ourselves: What will I eat? What will I drink? What will I wear? These three questions are sandwiched between a command—“do not be anxious” (Matt. 6:31)—and the keys to not worrying about our needs being met. Those keys are: (1) Trust that God knows we need “all these things” (v. 32). (2) Seek God’s kingdom, meaning we love God above all, and we love others the same way and amount we love ourselves. We don’t do this with a bad attitude but with willing hearts, letting love lead the way in our thoughts, words, and actions (Matt. 22:36-40). (3) Remember that, when you trust God and seek His kingdom, “all these things will be added to you” (v. 33).

The cause of our doubt and uncertainty about how our needs will be met is ultimately a lack of faith in who God is—a good and loving Father, who wants to provide for His children. While God knows we will struggle and suffer in this life, He promises to care for us through it all. So, we don’t worry about what’s ahead; we don’t have to let anxiety overtake our faith. Instead, we trust that God means what He says and that He will take care of us because He is faithful.
content.zh-Hant:
今天，我們常常難以分辨想要甚麼和需要甚麼。舊衣服或鞋子仍然合身，只是不再流行，我們便可能說自己需要新的；我們也可能說自己需要智慧型手機、社群媒體、在舊車漆剝落但仍能正常行駛時換一輛新車，或用最喜歡的汽水代替水。然而，回到基本層面，我們的需要其實很簡單：食物、水、住處、衣物、睡眠和休息，以及與他人的連結。

耶穌用我們問自己的三個問題概括我們的需要：我吃甚麼？我喝甚麼？我穿甚麼？這三個問題夾在一個命令——「不要憂慮」（馬太福音 6:31）——和不為需要能否得到滿足而憂慮的關鍵之間。這些關鍵是：（1）相信神知道我們需要「這一切東西」（32節）。（2）尋求神的國，也就是愛神勝過一切，並像愛自己一樣愛人。我們不是帶著不好的態度去做，而是甘心樂意，讓愛引導我們的思想、言語和行動（馬太福音 22:36-40）。（3）記得當你信靠神、尋求祂的國，「這些東西都要加給你們了」（33節）。

我們對需要如何得到滿足感到懷疑和不安，根本原因是對神的身分缺乏信心——祂是一位良善慈愛的父，願意供應兒女的需要。雖然神知道我們在今生會有掙扎和苦難，祂應許在這一切當中照顧我們。因此，我們不必為前路憂慮，也不必讓焦慮勝過信心。我們要相信神所說的都是真實可靠的，並相信祂必定照顧我們，因為祂是信實的。

question.en: What are some wants you tend to view as needs? Why is knowing the difference important?
question.zh-Hant: 有哪些你想要的東西，常被你當作必需品？為甚麼知道兩者的分別很重要？

question.en: What would it look like to trust God to meet your needs? How could that be difficult for you?
question.zh-Hant: 信靠神滿足你的需要會是甚麼樣子？這對你可能有甚麼困難？

prayer.en: God, thank You for being my Provider. Forgive me for the moments when I wonder if You’ll take care of me, and remind me of how You’ve taken care of me in the past.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢作我的供應者。當我懷疑祢是否會照顧我時，求祢赦免我，並提醒我祢過去如何照顧我。
